correctness.rationale: Directly reconstructed the sign-preservation lemma: writing q=sum w_j u_(j-1), next score q' differs by w1*sigma + sum_(j=1)^(L-1)(w_(j+1)-w_j)u_(j-1)-wL*u_(L-1). For sigma=+ the lower bound q'-q>=w1-sum(w_j-w_(j+1))-wL=0, and for - the reverse bound, so tie-breaking by the NEW current symbol preserves sigma. Induction gives constant emission; after t steps state has t new signs followed by the original prefix, yielding exact settling time. Global negation swaps equal-size basins. The sharp maximum follows from whether some initial sign can disagree with weighted-majority sign. Uniform count fixes first disagreeing index and counts remaining positive bits by binomial tails with even-length tie adjustment. final_claim: For deterministic binary memory shift F(u)=(sgn_{u0}(sum_{j=1}^L w_j u_{j-1}),u0,...,u_{L-2}) with nonnegative nonincreasing weights w1>=...>=wL, every future emitted bit equals its first sign, so exactly two fixed attractors have 2^(L-1) states each. Exact least settling time is L minus first disagreement index (0 for constant). Max settles in L iff w1<sum of remaining weights (otherwise L-1 for L>=2; L=1 gives 0). In uniform weights full binomial settling-time histogram holds, with a (1,2) two-cycle outside the monotone cone.
